drhp.business: The Company manufactures premium-quality 100% cotton combed and carded yarn, including hosiery/warp, conventional, organic and Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) yarn, across various count ranges, using Ring Spinning and Open-End Spinning capabilities. It caters to home textiles, weaving, denim and hosiery manufacturers across Maharashtra, Gujarat and other parts of India, and also serves customers in Asian and European countries. During FY2025-26 the Company took steps to diversify into the healthcare-related textile segment through its Surgical Cotton business, and per the Chairman's letter is also engaged in manufacturing cotton bales, oil cake and oilseeds.
drhp.end_markets: Maharashtra|Gujarat|other parts of India|Asian countries|European countries|home textiles manufacturers|weaving manufacturers|denim manufacturers|hosiery manufacturers
drhp.expansion: The Company is planning to expand its spinning division through installation of additional Ring Frames within its existing manufacturing premises, for which the required building infrastructure is already available. Separately, during FY2025-26 the Company commenced commercial production of Surgical Cotton, diversifying into the healthcare-related textile segment, and introduced a new product, 'OJAS COTTON ROLL', in August 2025. The Chairman's letter also notes the Company is evaluating replacement and upgradation of its existing manufacturing setup with advanced technology.

risks.note: Cotton is a principal raw material; prices are influenced by domestic/international demand-supply, crop production, climatic conditions, government policies, minimum support prices and global commodity prices. Significant fluctuations can affect production costs, inventory valuation and operating margins.

The Company is exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations, particularly against the US Dollar and other major currencies, to the extent of export sales, imports and other foreign-currency transactions, which may impact realisations and profitability.

The textile industry is highly competitive, with competition from organised and unorganised domestic manufacturers as well as international producers; increased capacities and aggressive pricing may pressure selling prices and margins.
Textile manufacturing is relatively energy intensive; a significant increase in electricity, fuel or other energy costs may adversely impact cost of production and profitability.
Global economic uncertainty, geopolitical conflicts, changes in international trade policies and supply-chain disruptions may affect export opportunities and overall industry conditions.

Operations are subject to environmental, labour, corporate, taxation, textile and other applicable laws; changes in the regulatory framework or compliance requirements may result in additional costs or operational requirements.
Demand and profitability in the textile sector may be affected by domestic and global economic cycles.

risks.note: Maximum exposure to credit risk arises primarily from trade receivables; the Company manages this through credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India's availability of raw materials, established manufacturing ecosystem, skilled workforce and large domestic market provide significant long-term opportunities to the textile sector.
- Growing demand for sustainable textiles, traceable raw materials, value-added yarns and technologically advanced textile products provides opportunities for manufacturers capable of maintaining consistent quality.
- Changes in global sourcing patterns may create opportunities for Indian textile manufacturers to establish relationships with international buyers seeking diversified sourcing destinations.
- The healthcare and medical consumables sector provides an opportunity to utilise cotton-processing knowledge while expanding into a different end-user industry, subject to successful commercialisation, regulatory requirements, market acceptance and operating conditions.
- Expansion of spinning capacities within the industry may lead to increased competition and pressure on margins.
- Management remains cautiously optimistic about medium- to long-term prospects while remaining mindful of volatility in cotton prices, energy costs, foreign exchange rates and global economic conditions.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company is planning to expand its spinning division through installation of additional Ring Frames within its existing manufacturing premises, for which the required building infrastructure is already available. Separately, during FY2025-26 the Company commenced commercial production of Surgical Cotton, diversifying into the healthcare-related textile segment, and introduced a new product, 'OJAS COTTON ROLL', in August 2025. The Chairman's letter also notes the Company is evaluating replacement and upgradation of its existing manufacturing setup with advanced technology.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Cotton is a principal raw material; prices are influenced by domestic/international demand-supply, crop production, climatic conditions, government policies, minimum support prices and global commodity prices. Significant fluctuations can affect production costs, inventory valuation and operating margins.
- The Company is exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations, particularly against the US Dollar and other major currencies, to the extent of export sales, imports and other foreign-currency transactions, which may impact realisations and profitability.
- The textile industry is highly competitive, with competition from organised and unorganised domestic manufacturers as well as international producers; increased capacities and aggressive pricing may pressure selling prices and margins.
- Textile manufacturing is relatively energy intensive; a significant increase in electricity, fuel or other energy costs may adversely impact cost of production and profitability.
- Global economic uncertainty, geopolitical conflicts, changes in international trade policies and supply-chain disruptions may affect export opportunities and overall industry conditions.
- Operations are subject to environmental, labour, corporate, taxation, textile and other applicable laws; changes in the regulatory framework or compliance requirements may result in additional costs or operational requirements.
- Demand and profitability in the textile sector may be affected by domestic and global economic cycles.
- Maximum exposure to credit risk arises primarily from trade receivables; the Company manages this through credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversification into the healthcare-related textile segment (Surgical Cotton), commenced commercial production in FY2025-26, intended to broaden the revenue base and reduce dependence on conventional cotton yarn products over the long term.
- Evaluating replacement and upgradation of existing manufacturing setup with advanced technology to enhance operational efficiency, product quality and competitiveness.
- Planning to expand the spinning division through installation of additional Ring Frames within existing manufacturing premises, for which building infrastructure is already available.
- Focus on increasing capacity utilisation, operational efficiency, cost optimisation, product quality, and customer diversification across domestic and export markets.
- Continued evaluation of opportunities for product innovation, value addition and development of specialised, higher-value textile products.
- Continues to explore opportunities to expand geographical reach and develop relationships with customers in domestic and export markets.
